citations.review_text: Whole lots of fun. It's very nostalgic to me as someone with a very well known liking to platform fighting games. It runs extremely smooth for someone with a not good computer/pc and I love that feature. Combos are very smooth to hit, unique character designs, and very good in anything else. I HIGHLY recommend this and ROA 2, but this one if you have a not so good computer for good frame rate.

For a game that's pretty close to Smash Bros. It still has quite enough to help it stand out compared to other competitors of the genre for sure. the Standard Stages, and Music are quite good, and Mod support is also good too.

Tetherball was also quite fun as well
Though if you use Mods, be sure your PC has some power, otherwise there will be slow motion.

Besides that note, definitely recommend.

Pretty cool game.

Best played irl, especially with mods.

Online is a mixed bag, but the netcode is overall tolerable.

There’s a special kind of fun to be had with friends just screwing around with the wackiest characters you could find on the workshop which is why even with the sequel out, I recommend picking this one up

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the extensive Steam Workshop support, which allows players to download custom characters, maps, and community-made content.

citations.review_text:
Super Fun Game.
Love playing this with my friend and I love getting all these cool addons of custom characters and maps.

The reason I personally love this game is because of the community workshop. The workshop allows users to create any desired character, and make a custom move set for that character, which anyone can use. An example would be sans with his custom bone attacks and gaster blaster. Also users can create custom maps. This game is similar to smash bros but with much more characters. I heavily recommend this game for all smash bros and fighting game lovers. The game is also super fun with friends. You and your friends could battle with Deltarune characters, or have crazy matchups like Ronald mc Donald vs Obama. Overall just a really fun fighting game with almost endless matchups, definitely recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as easy to control while offering a high skill ceiling that requires significant practice to master.

citations.review_text: One of the best fighting games out there. Easy to control, hard to master, and oh my god does it have insane workshop support. I was gifted this game by a friend of mine, and after a ton of hours I was amazed at what all can be done in here! 100/10, would fight again! :3

While appearing as just a simple pixel art platform fighter on the outside, delving into Rivals of Aether reveals one of the most fun experiences I have ever had with a game of this genre. Freedom of movement and the high ceiling for player expression is RoA's greatest strength. What is the game's expression without the colorful cast of rivals crafted to fit many playstyles. Add in customization for each profile and the endless possibilities to be made with the massive and passionate RoA workshop wraps this entire package with a gold ribbon for anyone to enjoy: casually or competitively.

cohorts.summary: Deep mechanical mastery and vast workshop content sustain long-term play despite sparse online queues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes a workshop feature allowing players to download and play as community-made custom characters, stages, and content.

citations.review_text: Lowkey super fun, I recommend the workshop feature is where alot of the fun comes from, but the main game is fun too!

Incredible platform fighter game engine. Base game is great but the workshop makes it incredible. I personally think this is better than Rivals 2 bc of how good the workshop is but that may change in the future.

Rivals of Aether is one of the best platform fighters I’ve played outside of Smash. It takes the core idea of that style of game and adds its own unique mechanics that make it stand out.

The gameplay is fast, smooth, and very skill-based. Movement feels great, and the lack of traditional shields puts more focus on positioning and timing, which makes matches feel more competitive.

Each character is unique and built around elemental themes, which gives the roster a lot of personality. Learning different characters feels rewarding, and there’s a good amount of depth for players who want to improve.

Another big highlight is the workshop support on PC. The community-made characters and content add a ton of replay value and keep the game feeling fresh.

Overall, Rivals of Aether is a fantastic platform fighter with strong mechanics and a lot of depth. It’s a great alternative for anyone looking for something similar to Smash but with its own identity. 

Gameplay: 9/10 Great | Overall: 9/10 Great

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that online player counts are low, making it difficult to find matches.

citations.review_text:
This game as some good makings to it but quite frankly has too many backwards ways of handling certain things. This game does expect precision on the part of the player but doesnt allow you to use the D pad for finer adjustments and it blocks out steam input and marks you trying to assign it with the games own controller changing system as futile.

Not to mention most of the characters are just simply unappealing from both a fun to play factor AND ESPECIALLY from a fun to fight aspect. The fact that this games endless mode has better ideas for their characters and they have decided to not implement them into the actual game shows you what you need to know because the developers have quite frankly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off to the sequel while this game is still quite buggy and prone to crashing.

The tutorial itself is buggy, let that set in. Not to mention the fact that the ranked & casual online spaces are ghost towns, most randos you do face online will whoop your ass 9 times out of 10 and the fact that the workshop content is far far FAR better than any basegame content says it all. 

If you do want to get this game, in short; just use workshop and only play with your friends.

Update: I have been playing this game further, and because there isnt that many people left, a lot of the people are very much above basic skill level. To the point where trying to be casual in...well the casual matchmaking mode feels like im playing ranked.
which, in short; is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hellish.

I don't feel like I should know every greasy lil nook & cranny inside & out in other to enjoy playing the game and not be dumpstered everytime I try.

Rivals of Aether is clearly designed to compete with Smash Brothers in every way except the casual experience. There is a strong emphasis on competitive integrity and efficiency. The online ranked mode, while not flawless, is a seamless illustration of how to battle online. The controls are crisp and responsive. The simplicity significantly adds to the experience as a competitive outlet.

Have you ever played Smash and felt like your controls weren't reacting the way you expected? If so, you should play Rivals of Aether instead. Character control is clean, every input is logically mapped and understand and a strong grasp of executing their functions will scratch the itch of fast-paced platform combat. RoA has streamlined the feeling, and playing anything else will feel clunky.

Online multiplayer is, admittedly, quite low in numbers now that Rivals of Aether 2 is out. However, grabbing someone from online and starting up some friendlies is so seamless and as long as you aren't living too far apart the lag is quite minimal. More important, the clean controls often correct reads your inputs in-spite of the lag and allows the game to continue without too much disturbances. Should you get lucky and be able to encounter some ranked opponents, it's quite satisfying to kick their ass in your climb to the top. Just be aware of GMs, they likely haven't showered in weeks and you can smell them even across the country.

I will admit that I am a little biased against Rivals here, but its casual experience is practically non-existent. The only reason it might be considered viable as a casual game is through workshop, which is a fun niche until the magic of playing Goku, Ronald McDonald, or 6-Pixel-PNG-Pete wears off. Workshop is great, but it's not a casual pick-up party game that Super Smash Brothers is.

Rivals is sweaty, it's competitive, and it's damn near impossible for a beginner to get into. But that's its goal as a game. You pick this up because you realize how ♥…

An incredibly fun game with 18 unique characters, beautiful pixel art and music, and elaborate combat. And if that's not enough, there's tonnes upon tonnes of workshop content. The only issue is the undeservedly low player count, making it difficult to find an online match.

The overall gameplay does feel good. Workshop characters also add an interesting dynamic, I even used workshop characters for abyss endless as well as workshop boss fights.

I'm used to having things like shields, so it felt very weird to not have shields in this game at all, and the bots will parry the crap out of you instead of shields, there is no grabs in the game either which that would have helped against the bots that endlessly spam parry.

What bums me out is that Abyss Endless is exclusively local, not available for online play, the story mode is very short, but I guess there's a challenge for you if you want to get gold medal on all the story levels, the achievements were also fun to get.

You can also get the gold skins for characters in ranked, I was told that if you hit gold rank on a character, you cannot fall below gold rank (so Gold 5 is the lowest gold rank), I guess they did this to prevent longtime players from defeating bronze players (which is also the lowest rank in the game and you start with it), though once you get to silver, you can face against gold players (ranked only allows you to fight against other players with an offset of -1 or +1 or equal), I guess this is kind of smart and cool, but this does mean the least experienced opponents you'll face are silver and the most experienced opponents are Platinum.

I recommend friends with this game still.
